info.title: Ductura API
info.description:
Shared errors: any route may answer these besides the errors listed under it.
- 500 internal: problem body {error, code, messageKey: "errors.internal", status, requestId}.
- 429 too_many_requests: problem body {error, code, messageKey: "errors.tooManyRequests", status, requestId}; header retry-after in whole seconds.

post.summary: OIDC back-channel logout: the provider posts a signed logout token, no cookie.

get.summary: Return from the identity provider; checks state and PKCE, opens the session.
Starts AAI@EduHr login (PKCE); returnTo is narrowed to a safe local path.

post.summary: Closes every session of the caller; on failure keeps the cookie.
Closes the current session. Same Origin only; an empty body.
Confirms the caller's security key against an assertion challenge. 403 for a key that is not the caller's or is revoked; 409 when the signature counter fell or stayed the same (0 to 0 is accepted).

400.description: content_length_invalid, content_length_mismatch, body_stream_error, invalid_json, challenge_invalid, ceremony_invalid

post.summary: A one-time challenge of 32 random bytes for one ceremony of this session, registration or assertion. It expires after timeoutMs and is spent by the first attempt, successful or not.

200.description: challenge issued; the purpose picks the shape

post.summary: Registers the caller's security key (ES256, COSE -7; attestation none) against a registration challenge; the key is the COSE key in authenticatorData. 403 when the account already has a key, 409 when the key is registered.

400.description: content_length_invalid, content_length_mismatch, body_stream_error, invalid_json, challenge_invalid, ceremony_invalid

post.summary: Records the client's environment (D-300): app, version, system, browser, device and a screen width class, each from a closed list. Works without a login, under the rate limit; the body is the JCS form of the value, and any other field, value or form is 400 invalid_input. Never used to decide access.

Comments on a work (B-10). The action picks the body: create {anchor, body, documentId} and reply {body, threadId} answer 200 {id}; resolve and reopen {threadId} and delete {commentId} answer 204; list {documentId} answers 200 {comments}. Exactly those keys, at most 16 KiB; an unknown action is 404. The database decides who may read or write (403); a thread that changed in the meantime is 409.

200.description: the new comment's id (create, reply) or the comments (list)

post.summary: Revision requests on a work (DAN-314). The action picks the body, as its exact JCS bytes, at most 16 KiB: create {anchor, documentId, instruction, requestedRevision} answers 200 {request_id, row_seq, version, state}; respond, accept, reopen, rereview and withdraw (with requestId and expectedSeq) answer 200 {outcome: "applied", row_seq, version, state}, or 409 {outcome: "conflict", row_seq, version, state} when expectedSeq is stale; list {documentId} answers 200 {requests}. A malformed id reads as a foreign one (403); a transition the state does not allow is 409 not_allowed; an unknown action is 404.

409.description: expectedSeq is stale: the current counter, version and state; not_allowed

get.summary: The desktop packages a client may offer: one row per system and architecture at most, by system then architecture. url is a path on this address or an https address; sha256 is the SHA-256 of the package bytes in lowercase hex, which the client checks before it opens the package. An empty list: no package yet. A manifest the server cannot read makes the answer 503, never a partial list.

200.description: manifest (an empty list when there is no package yet)

post.summary: One evidence segment and the document after it. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1` (signed now, 200) or `2` (signed by the worker: 202 pending_signature, then the same request again).

202.description: stored, receipt pending_signature (protocol 2 only); not an acknowledgement

post.summary: The caller's own work for one assignment and its current revision; `start: true` makes it. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1`; anyone but the student gets 404.

One page of the replay of a work: the verified stored bytes of its segments in chain order, as the JCS text of the page. The body is exactly {documentId, from: 0} for the first page and {documentId, from, head} for every later one, with the head the first page reported; any other shape is 422. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1`. A work the caller may not read, an id that cannot exist or a page past the end is 404. A record that no longer ends at `head` is 409 record_changed (read again from the first page); a record that does not verify is 503, never a partial page.

200.description: one page, its JCS text unchanged

post.summary: The student acknowledges the notice of an assignment version they were shown. The body is exactly {versionNo, fingerprint}: the version and the SHA-256 the browser computed of the notice text, at most 1 KiB, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only), with no escape and no repeated key. A malformed assignment id is 400 invalid_assignment_id, judged before the session. A version that is no longer current is 409 conflict; a stored notice other than the one shown is 409 notice_changed, and nothing is recorded.

A teacher of the assignment publishes its next version against the version they saw: {expectedVersion} and the whole content, both word bounds named (null drops one), at most 90 000 bytes. A tightening of the rules, an AI purpose under a prohibited policy, wordMin above wordMax or an impossible date is 422; a stale version is 409 version_conflict, and of two requests with the same version one writes.

A teacher creates a course in their institution: exactly {name, academicYear, aiPolicy}, at most 2 KiB, sent as application/json (only the media type before any parameter is judged). The name is 1 to 160 UTF-16 units with no space at either end; the academic year is two consecutive years such as 2026/2027. The same course sent again answers its id, never a second course.
A teacher of the course revokes its enrolment code. The body is exactly {}; revoked is false when there was no code to revoke.

A teacher of the course issues its enrolment code, valid until {validUntil}, replacing any earlier one; at most 1 KiB. The instant keeps its offset and fraction as sent; an impossible date or one the database refuses is 422.

Enrols the caller in the course of a code. The body is exactly {code}, at most 64 UTF-16 units and 1 KiB, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). A wrong or expired code is 422 refused; too many guesses are 429 too_many_attempts, and each guess counts even when refused.

An administrator of the institution confirms one candidate as a teacher. The body is exactly {}. A caller who is not an administrator is 403; for an administrator every candidate that cannot be confirmed (themself, another institution's, a missing one, one whose last login gave no right) is the same 404.

An administrator of the institution ends one person's confirmed teacher role. The body is exactly {}; revoked is false when that person holds no active confirmed teacher role in the caller's institution, so another institution's person looks the same as a missing one.
A teacher of the course ends one student's membership. The body is exactly {}; removed is false when that user holds no open student membership there.
A teacher of the course lets one removed student enrol again; the student still needs a valid code. The body is exactly {}; allowed is false when nothing was blocking that student there.
One work's exception from the language of its assignment, keyed by the student; {language: null} removes it. At most 128 bytes. Answers the language the work has afterwards.

200.description: the language the work has now

post.summary: A teacher of the assignment sets the language its works are written in, against the version they saw: {expectedVersion, language}, at most 128 bytes, sent as application/json (only the media type before any parameter is judged). A malformed assignment id is 422; a stale version or a work already asked to be submitted is 409 conflict. Answers the new version.

The same exception keyed by the work's document id, so the student's id never reaches the browser; a document that is not a work of this teacher's assignment is refused like another teacher's (403). A malformed document id is 422, judged after the content type and the body.

200.description: the language the work has now

get.summary: The last published state of a work, the same bytes and ETag for the owner and the teacher. The request carries `ductus-protocol: 1` (and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin when the browser sends it), else 403; a teacher's read writes the access log. `If-None-Match: "<etag>"` with the ETag last read answers 304. After the submission the bytes are the submitted revision, marked `ductus-live-state: submitted`. 204 when nothing is published yet.

304.description: the state of the ETag sent

put.summary: Publishes the last state of a work (the student owner only). The body is the exact JCS bytes of a valid document snapshot, at most 2 MiB. The request carries exactly one precondition: `If-None-Match: *` for the first write or `If-Match: "<token>"` with the last token, else 428. 200 {outcome, token} when accepted or unchanged; 409 {outcome: "conflict", token} with the current token (null when nothing is published yet) when the token is stale. The session is checked before the first body byte.

200.description: accepted, or the same state again

409.description: the token is stale: the current one, null when nothing is published

get.summary: The operator's read of the log: the records of a window, at most 1000 a page, in seq order, each as the operator read (operator_log) masks it (an address only as a network: the host part is always cut, a mask longer than /24 for IPv4 or /48 for IPv6 is cut to it, a shorter one such as /8 stays; no token, cookie or session value; a value the read cannot vouch for is "hidden"). The pipeline decides who reaches it, before the route: 403 forbidden from a network outside the list (step 3), or for an account not on the operator list of the server or without a confirmed second factor (step 8); 401 unauthenticated without a live session (step 8). from and to are UTC instants of the calendar, the window is from inclusive to exclusive, from before to and at most 24 hours apart (exactly 24 is allowed); after is the seq the page starts after (0 by default), at most 2^53-1. A repeated or unknown parameter, or a window outside these bounds, is 422 and reads nothing. next is the seq of the last event when the page is full (1000), to pass as after, and may then lead to an empty page; null when the page is shorter. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503, never a shorter page.

200.description: a page of events, possibly none

get.summary: Liveness: the process answers. Reads no database, session or environment.

200.description: alive. Since 1.3.0 also the state of the main database (`state`, checked with a time limit) and the versions; never an address, a name or an error.

state.description: degraded: the main database is not ok or did not answer in time

minClientVersion.description: oldest client version this server serves

get.summary: Readiness per capability, closed words only.
Public status in three parts, closed words, nothing about a person.
The caller's saved interface language, or null.

post.summary: Saves the caller's interface language. Canonical JSON, nothing but the locale.

The process summary of one work, built from the accepted evidence only, as its JCS bytes. The body is exactly {documentId}, at most 1 KiB; any other key is 422. A work the caller may not read, or that does not exist, is 404; a record that does not verify is 503, never a partial summary.

get.summary: The settings catalogue: every key, the levels that may hold it, its kind, default and hard limits.

The rows of one level in the caller's scope (course names the course for the course level and is absent for every other), and for every catalogue key of that level the value that holds without it (source: a higher level or default) and the narrowest higher bound. A level or course that is not the caller's gives 404, the same as a course that does not exist (C-23: another's is nonexistent).

200.description: the level's rows and what it inherits

put.summary: Sets the caller's value and bound of one key at one level (the bound as locked, min and max); no value and no bound remove the row and the level above holds again. course is a course id for the course level and null for every other. A level or course that is not the caller's gives 404, the same as a course that does not exist. A key outside the catalogue, a level the catalogue does not allow for it, a value of the wrong kind or out of its limits and a bound of a wrong shape give 422; crossing a higher bound gives 409. A refusal of the catalogue (422) comes before the level check (404), as in settings.set_value. 409 needs a key a lower level holds under a higher bound; the first catalogue has none, so its vector shows the shape only. Every change is kept with its author, time, old and new value.

200.description: saved (changed is false when the row already held it)

get.summary: Who opened the caller's own work and when (PRODUCT §5 rule 17): one entry per stored opening of five minutes, newest first; the client groups them into Europe/Zagreb days. No total of visits and no duration (D-274 MQ10). The query names the oldest entry shown, beforeAt and beforeId from next; a page from it holds only windows strictly older. Only both together, on the five-minute grid, a lowercase UUID, not in the future and not before year one are a cursor; anything else, and any other parameter, reads the first page with continued false, never an error, so every opening stays reachable. Another's work, an unknown and a malformed id read the same 404 (C-23). A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

200.description: a page of openings, possibly none

get.summary: The state of the caller's own work for every assignment student.assignments.get would list at the same instant: one row per assignment, by assignmentId (lowercase). submitted: the caller has a recorded submission for the assignment, of any of its versions; in_progress: the caller has a work for it (one per student and assignment) and no recorded submission; not_started: no work. The two reads are separate, so a client joins them by lowercase id and shows no state for an assignment without a row on both sides. The identity comes from the session only. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503, never a partial list.

200.description: ready (an empty list when the student has no course)

get.summary: The courses of the caller's open student memberships and the current version of every assignment in each. Courses by name (hr collation), then id; assignments by due time, then id. The identity comes from the session only.

200.description: ready (an empty list when the student has no course)

post.summary: The student submits the revision they saw: exactly {documentId, revision}, at most 1 KiB; no time, text of the work or hash comes from the client. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1`. The database clock at the click is the time; the revision is reconstructed and, only when it matches, the submission is recorded and its signed receipt returned. The first click binds: another revision later is 409 already_requested. Another student's or a missing work is 404. 503 carries the stage and `retry-after: 5`.

Sends a problem report: the user's description and a closed technical context. The body is the JCS form of the value, at most 8 KiB; the description is 1 to 1000 code points, no lone surrogate, with a visible character and no control or bidi character other than newline and tab (checked by the server, answered 422). The route is a page template; the server checks it against its closed list of 27 templates and answers 422 otherwise. At most five reports per account in an hour.

201.description: recorded; the reference the user quotes

get.summary: Whether the caller may see the teacher pages: a confirmed and unrevoked institution role (institution.actor_has_role('teacher')), never the login claims. The session and the role come from one snapshot, so denied is always an open session without the role and allowed always comes with a signed-in principal. scope is principalScope, for the shell of the teacher pages only; it is not the general source of the principal. No session is 401, a database that cannot be asked 503. Names no course, assignment or count: the role alone gives no access to a work (C-23).

post.summary: teacher.submissions.get for many assignments in one snapshot (R1): one entry per distinct id, lowercase, in the order of first appearance. POST so the ids never land in a URL; the body is exactly {assignmentIds}, 0 to 500 UUIDs in any case (duplicates count), at most 32 KiB; any other key or a malformed id is 422 invalid_input. An assignment the caller does not teach, or that does not exist, is the same entry with an empty list, never 403 or 404; proving that over the database belongs to the handler. More than 500 assignments take several reads, each its own snapshot. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

200.description: an entry per assignment, possibly with no rows

get.summary: The teacher's courses and their assignments (institution.list_teacher_courses). Courses by academic year descending, then name (hr collation), then id; assignments by due time, then title, then id. Each course carries its rule on AI help, which a new assignment may only keep or narrow.

post.summary: The teacher's fast path through the works of one assignment (B-11, #757): per student the state of the work, its text as blocks and the same process summary the student sees. POST so the assignment id never lands in a URL; the body is exactly {assignmentId}, a UUID in any case, at most 1 KiB; any other key or a malformed id is 422 invalid_input. An assignment the caller does not teach, or that does not exist, is the same empty list, never 403 or 404. Named students by surname, given name (hr) and id, then the unnamed by id.

get.summary: One open mentorship of the caller as mentor. Another institution's, an ended one, an unknown and a malformed id all read the same 404.
The open mentorships of the caller as mentor, newest first; anyone else gets the same empty list. No time, activity or count of a work.

Which students of an assignment submitted, with the work each row links to, for the assignment's teacher; one row per student with an open membership, by student id. Anyone else, an unknown or a malformed id gets the same empty list. No text, name, exact time, deadline, hash or submission id.
